note: Grand Mesa NF, ~10,500 ft, single loop in Engelmann spruce between Weir & Johnson and Sackett reservoirs; some sites overlook one or the other. Non-motorized boating and fishing. Mosquitoes plentiful. Reached by gravel forest roads (FR 521, then FR 126 2.8 mi) from Collbran; a firsthand reviewer says only a few sites fit rigs over 25 ft. --Claude
summary: FS page (updated Sept 17, 2026) + recreation.gov (10165731, FCFS Scan & Pay listing, no rates): confirmed 11 sites, max spur 33, vault toilet, no water, FCFS, $16 (+$8 vehicle); added season June 26 - Sept 22, firewood, day use. Note cleaned of field facts; road wording reduced to what sources support.
flags: Phone: none stored. Grand Valley Ranger District, 1010 Kimball Avenue, Grand Junction, (970) 242-8211 (GMUG offices page; the campground page itself lists only the Supervisor's Office 970-874-6600). recreation.gov's (928) 537-8888 / camping@rrmofa.com is the concessionaire's (rrmofa.com).

Road: the FS page has no road or RV wording beyond the directions ('take County Road 58 south 1.9 miles. Turn left at the "T" for 5.8 miles to Forest Road #521 ... Continue straight on Forest Road #521 for about 7.2 miles to junction with Forest Road #126. Turn left at Weir and Johnson Campground sign and go 2.8 miles to the campground.'). The FS road atlas has FR 126 'WEIR & JOHNSON CG' as maintenance level 4 'moderate degree of user comfort', crushed aggregate/gravel, 2.97 mi. The old note's 'long, dusty, bumpy gravel road' and 'only a few sites fit rigs over 25 ft' are a reviewer's words, not the agency's; the latter kept in the note as attributed. Max spur 33 > 23; no criteria problem, no 4WD wording.

Status: the FS page shows a 'Site Closed' banner, which matches its stated season end (Sept 22): ordinary seasonal closing. The page's forest-wide alert (Gold Mountain Wildfire closure order v4.0) is on the Ouray Ranger District (Dexter Creek / Cutler roads), not Grand Mesa; no closure applies to this campground's roads.

Waterfront 'lakeview' kept (checked both ways): on NAIP the loop sits on the spruce neck between the two reservoirs. The west-side spurs are ~20-25 m from the western reservoir's shore and the north/east spurs ~25-30 m from the eastern one, but a continuous band of spruce stands between every spur and the water; no open apron. FS 'Some sites overlook one or the other reservoir.' Lakefront not earned.
